## Claims
- [computed] For \(i=j=p=2,c=6\), the accepted \(c=6\) Pieri/Smith output has quotient ranks \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\), respectively, and rank \(0\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,32\), with no torsion. Hence
  \[
  Q=J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6.
  \]
  [artifact 162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126]
- [source-backed] With \(r=8,n-r=4,i=j=2\), one has \(a=\min(4-2,8-2)=2\), \(b=2\); the two source families generate \(J\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}=6\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [proved] The two generating families specialize to
  \[
  \mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},
  \qquad
  \mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
  \]
  Since either six-element family generates \(J\), it induces a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, its images are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\); therefore no proper subfamily generates \(J\).
- [proved] The requested new \(i=j=p=2,c=6\) minimality corollary is established: both \(\mathcal F_{\rm top}\) and \(\mathcal F_{\rm bot}\) are minimal generating sets of \(J\).

## Strategy
Sum the accepted degreewise ranks, then apply source-stated generation and the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion.
